summary: ELI LILLY AND COMPANY (LEI: FRDRIPF3EKNDJ2CQJL29) is identifier-confirmed, registered in Indiana, United States, with cross-references to OpenCorporates (us_in/183025-143) and Wikidata (Q632240). Per GLEIF, the entity's ultimate parent is recorded under a reporting exception indicating ownership by one or more natural persons, leaving the beneficial ownership chain opaque; this constitutes a medium-confidence structural risk signal requiring further review. Key officers identified via OpenCorporates include David Ricks (officer from 2025-01-23) and Jonathan Haug (senior managing official from 2023-05-25), with David A. Ricks also reported as CEO and board member since 2017 per Wikidata; GLEIF records several direct accounting-consolidation subsidiaries including LILLY VENTURES FUND I LLC, ELI LILLY KINSALE LIMITED, and Lilly Nederland Finance B.V., among others. Three related-party risk signals warrant attention: board member Katherine Baicker is a possible name match — unconfirmed by birth date or nationality — with a PEP record on OpenSanctions and a political office-holder record on EveryPolitician (both medium confidence); officer Patrik Jonsson is similarly a possible name match only with PEP and political office-holder records on the same sources (medium confidence); and officer Christopher Anderson matches records in both the Panama Papers and the Paradise Papers (Appleby) at ICIJ score 100/100 (high confidence), though this is a name-level match against a related party and does not constitute a finding of wrongdoing. A material gap exists: Wikirate could not be queried due to a source API schema error, so any data that source would have contributed is unavailable.

One board member record in the packet (f12) is identified only by a Wikidata QID (Q105798427) with no resolved name, representing an unresolved person in the governance record.

All three related-party risk signals (r6–r11) are name-match-only findings with no corroborating identifiers (birth date, nationality) to confirm identity; they require further investigation but are not positive identifications.
GLEIF subsidiary relationships are reported at medium confidence and reflect accounting consolidation as reported to GLEIF, not independently verified ownership structures.
